notPublished.read: DoH Annual Report and Accounts 2024-25 (186pp). Searched for voluntary, grants, SPPG, Family Support, Parentline and Sure Start. There is no voluntary or community sector expenditure line and no SPPG payments to the VCS. 'Voluntary' appears only in narrative and turnover. The Core Grant total comes from press releases, not the accounts.

PHA Annual Report and Accounts 2024-25. The 'Management of Contracts with the Community and Voluntary Sector' section (PDF p.62-63) is about governance and procurement only: no money total and no children's or families split. The commissioning note splits only General Medical Services / Other providers / R&D capital grants. One narrative mention: a small grants programme for 17 projects in universities, colleges and training providers, with no amount.

2024-25 ARA Note 3: purchase of care from non-HSC bodies is not split into voluntary and private. No grants-to-voluntary line and no children's split. Sure Start appears only once, in the internal audit table (PDF p.88): 'Management of Contracts with Voluntary Sector Organisations (including sure start schemes)'. This is the only trust document that ties Sure Start schemes to voluntary-sector contracts. It gives no amount.

2024-25 accounts Note 3: purchase of care is not split. No voluntary grants line, no children's split, and no Sure Start mention in the accounts. The internal audit table lists 'Management of Contracts with Voluntary Organisations' (satisfactory) with no amount.

2024-25 ARA Note 3: purchase of care is not split. No voluntary grants line. Sure Start is mentioned only as Trust 'Sure Start and Family Support teams' (PDF p.67), with no amount and no statement that it goes to voluntary lead bodies. Internal audit gave 'Contracts with Voluntary / Community Organisations' Part Satisfactory and Part Limited assurance (PDF p.85-86), because payments are not linked to reported activity.

2024-25 ARA Note 3: purchase of care is not split, and there is no voluntary grants line. Sure Start appears only in the segment description: 'Family support, Early Years, Health visiting and school nursing are included together with all Sure Start Projects' (PDF p.158), inside the Children & Young People's directorate. There is no amount and no statement that it goes to voluntary lead bodies.

2024-25 ARA has a voluntary grants line (see figures), but purchase of care is not split and there is no children's split. Sure Start appears only in the segment description of the Children & Families directorate, in the same wording as Southern (PDF p.145). There is no amount and no lead-body statement.

YJA Annual Report and Accounts 2024-25 (https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2025-07/2024-25%20Annual%20Report%20and%20Accounts%20-%20Youth%20Justice%20Agency.PDF). Note 2 Programme expenditure has no grants line; 'Contracted out and managed services' is 85 £000 and is not attributed to the VCS. The procurement section lists 'external funding to voluntary and community groups, small grants' as a category it reviews, but gives no amount anywhere.

DoJ ARA 2024-25: no VCS-only total and no named grants to NIACRO, Include Youth or Community Restorative Justice. There is only 'Other grants' (public, private and voluntary together, recorded above), and a commitments note that mentions 'funding payable to certain voluntary and community sector organisations' inside a mixed £5.182m total.

DE ARA 2024-25 (170 pp., posted 2026-07): no 'grants to voluntary bodies' line. The grants note has one 'Grants' line (3,593,195 £000 core / 655,546 group), mostly to EA and schools. No separate Sure Start, Pathway or Toybox figure. A Toybox amount was found nowhere (press releases, WMS 2024-25, AQW deposited paper). Sure Start lead bodies by type are not in the accounts or the infographic.

PEG voluntary vs private split: not given by the EA ARA 2024-25 or by DE. Extended Schools: the EA ARA mentions only an internal audit (limited assurance), gives no amount, and the money goes to schools. T:BUC camps: not in the EA ARA (the award list is on eanifunding.org.uk instead).

DfC ARA 2024-25 does not itemise the Regional Infrastructure Support Programme, Neighbourhood Renewal or Advice; it has only the 'Community and Voluntary Sector Funding' estimate line (recorded above). NICVA State of the Sector's latest Government Funding Database totals are for 2021-22; no 2024-25 GFD total was found.

TEO ARA 2024-25: no VCS-only grants total. T:BUC camps are given only as a budget, and Urban Villages only as capital grants. The Earmarked Funds table (T:BUC/Shared Future) extracts too badly to attribute values to years.

Statement of Accounts 2024-25 (minutes.belfastcity.gov.uk s125248), full text: the expenditure-by-nature note has no grants line; there are only related-party grants (£2,894,252) and REFCUS capital grant aid, which is not separated. The Financial performance 2024-25 web page has no grants figure. No 2024-25 grants register covering all programmes was found; programme-level lists exist in committee papers (CSP above). No children's or youth programme line was found.

Signed certified accounts 2024-25 (antrimandnewtownabbey.gov.uk .../signed-certified-accounts-2024-25.aspx), full text: no grants line in expenditure-by-nature; the related party note (p.118) gives no grants figure. A web search found no 2024-25 recipient list.
Financial statements YE 31 March 2025: no total grants line, only the related-party £578k. The grants page lists schemes; no 2024-25 recipient list was found.
Statement of accounts as at 31 March 2025: no total grants figure (the narrative says grant funding is provided, with no amount); only the related-party £459,442. No 2024-25 recipient list was found.
DCSDC 31/03/25 audited financial statements: no grants total, only related-party payments. Grants run through the dcsdc.gograntaid.com portal; no published 2024-25 award list was found.

FODC signed financial statements 31 March 2025 (https://www.fermanaghomagh.com/app/uploads/2025/09/FODC-Signed-Financial-Statements-31-March-2025.pdf): the narrative mentions 'direct support including a grants programme' with no figure. The related party note (p.105) gives £1,096k of transactions with 22 bodies and £43k of 'works/grants' to companies with councillor interests; neither is a grants total. No recipient list was found.
MEA statement of accounts YE 31 March 2025: no grants line. The related-party table lists payments over £3,000 to named bodies without a grants total. No recipient list was found.
MUDC Statement of Accounts 2024-25: no total grants line (related-party £152,200 only).
Statement of accounts YE 31 March 2025, a scan read from page images (contents, narrative pp.3-10, notes pp.103-115): no grants total; related-party grants/SLAs only.

LCCC 2024-25 final accounts: no audited grants note. There is only the narrative '£994k in community grant funding' and a related-party table of grants to member-linked bodies (p.90), whose total could not be extracted cleanly.

PCSP Annual Effectiveness Report 2024-25 (Joint Committee) and the 2024-25 annual reports for the AN, AND, ABC, Belfast, CCG, DCS, MEA and MU PCSPs: no regional figure for funding paid to community groups. AN, ABC, Belfast (only '£846,517 – Administration and Operational Budget'), MEA (operational spend £250,419.20, not split by recipient) and MU give no community-group grant total. The FO, LC and NMD PCSP 2024-25 annual reports were not on pcsps.org and were not read.
